items.problem: Bootstrap omitted csproj-linked shared XAML, code, resource dictionaries, and assets; this led to manual reconstruction, duplicate type/XAML errors, a missing-style startup crash, and loss of source theme/branding.
items.evidence: session-log.txt lines 123-151 report only 6 copied files; the source csproj links App.xaml, MainPage.xaml/.cs, Styles.xaml, scenario XAML, and assets. Turns 11-19 reconstruct files manually; lines 2927-2953 show duplicate/XAML errors; lines 4115-4190 show the startup crash and missing Styles.xaml.
items.skill_search: Searched Initialize-UwpMigration.ps1 and skill docs for Link, linked, and SharedContent; no linked-item handling existed.
items.root_cause: Initialize-UwpMigration.ps1 used only a recursive filesystem crawl rooted at -Source, so MSBuild items outside that folder were invisible.
items.proposed_fix: Resolve declared Compile/ApplicationDefinition/Page/Content/AppxManifest items with Link metadata, expand common project properties, copy them to Link paths, then include them in rewrite/triage/mapping.
items.generalizes: Legacy UWP solutions commonly centralize shell XAML, styles, code-behind, and branded assets in shared folders via linked project items.

items.problem: The skill prescribed a nonexistent winapp build command.
items.evidence: session-log.txt lines 2827-2893: winapp rejected build; lines 2895-2914 show the agent switching to dotnet build.
items.skill_search: winapp build appeared in SKILL.md Step 3, build discipline, final build, and the validator header.
items.root_cause: The documentation assumed a winapp subcommand not present in the installed CLI.
items.proposed_fix: Use explicit `dotnet build <project.csproj> -p:Platform=x64` throughout and state that winapp has no build command.
items.generalizes: Every migration follows the same compile loop and otherwise loses time before receiving any source diagnostic.

items.problem: The threading replacement used an unqualified DispatcherQueue name that becomes ambiguous in files retaining Windows.System.
items.evidence: session-log.txt lines 2929-2930: CS0104 between Microsoft.UI.Dispatching.DispatcherQueue and Windows.System.DispatcherQueue; turn 23 fixes it by fully qualifying the type.
items.skill_search: MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md threading showed unqualified DispatcherQueue calls and had no CS0104 warning.
items.root_cause: Many Windows API samples import Windows.System for User and Launcher APIs, exposing a second DispatcherQueue type.
items.proposed_fix: Show the fully qualified Microsoft.UI.Dispatching.DispatcherQueue and document the Windows.System collision.
items.generalizes: Windows.System imports are common in UWP samples that also require UI-thread dispatch.

items.problem: Manifest guidance preferred scaffold branding, and shell conversion did not require preservation of RequestedTheme, visible window title, or custom title-bar icon.
items.evidence: migration-score.json marks all 3 features partial; discrepancies.json reports dark UWP versus light WinUI and source title/icon versus scaffold values. Final MainWindow.xaml retained Title/UserInfo, TitleBar/UserInfo, and Assets/AppIcon.ico.
items.skill_search: RequestedTheme and window title were absent; MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md explicitly called scaffold image references preferred.
items.wrong_text_if_any: Preferred - keep the scaffold's manifest image references.
items.root_cause: The skill prioritized launch-safe template assets but lacked a shell identity parity pass.
items.proposed_fix: Preserve source RequestedTheme and display name, apply the name to Window/custom TitleBar, prefer resolvable source branding, and reject scaffold project-name/placeholder icon values.
items.generalizes: Every scaffold introduces default theme, title, and icon values that can silently replace the source app identity.

items.problem: The validator warned on the initializer's own empty deferred-file sentinel.
items.evidence: session-log.txt lines 3400-3406, 3584-3590, and 4507-4513 show the warning despite zero deferred mapping rows.
items.skill_search: Initialize-UwpMigration.ps1 writes '| (none) | - |'; Validate-UwpMigration.ps1 recognized only the phrase 'No items deferred'.
items.wrong_text_if_any: Validator empty-state check did not accept the initializer's generated table sentinel.
items.root_cause: Producer and consumer used different representations for an empty deferred list.
items.proposed_fix: Accept the '(none)' row as the empty sentinel.
items.generalizes: Every migration with no deferred files otherwise emits a misleading consistency warning.
